page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-48GB is a virtual server belonging to the Cloud Native family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core, 16 MB of L3 cache, and 48.0 GB of RAM, which provides a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per core. This server does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it is provisioned with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a split profile. The server demonstrates strong single-core capabilities in Geekbench, scoring 2114.0 (top 25%), and performs well in text processing tasks. However, due to its shared CPU allocation, raw computational performance is limited, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core benchmarks falling into the bottom 10% and 25% respectively. Memory performance also varies; while small-block cached read bandwidth is average at 411.75 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths are weak, placing in the bottom 25%.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server offers a high density of memory relative to its shared CPU resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, high-performance CPU execution. It is suitable for caching layers, text processing, and lightweight web serving. However, its weak database operations benchmark and lower uncached memory bandwidth suggest it is less optimal for heavy, high-throughput transactional databases.
